compute.note: Parameters: 64 from the method string (high confidence); the circuit code builds 64 one-parameter gates (SU2_symmetrized._get_dimerizarion_layers: range(1) x 4 shifts x (8 + 8) pairs), which reproduces it. Iterations: 2000 = 1000 natural-gradient steps without symmetry projection, then 1000 continuing with the 128-element projector (n_iter default 1000; main.py is called twice and passes only lr). As published, Optimizer.optimize() ends with "return res.x" on the circuit object, which has no attribute x, so the first call exits with an AttributeError and "&&" would skip the symmetric run; the step counts are therefore what the code intends, not what it can be shown to have run, hence confidence low. Samples: none; the method string says exact gradients on a state vector. The code has no exact branch that main.py reaches: it draws binomial estimates with the default 2^36 shots (--log2samples default 36), which is exact to about 4e-6 relative. Provenance: the value entered VarBench in ee77630 (2022-09-07, Nikita Astrakhantsev); the program was added to methods in 6887677 (2024-08-10) ("wip: added the VQE simulator"; next commit "VQE simulator: dusted-off version runs"), so it is a later reconstruction. The VarBench SM (arXiv:2302.04919 Sec. S3 D) describes the ansatz and the natural-gradient update but no step count. No device or time is recorded.

compute.note: parameters = alpha N^2 + alpha N + N = 1*16^2 + 1*16 + 16 = 288 real (float32) parameters: nk.models.RBM is a dense RBM (Dense kernel N x alpha N, hidden bias alpha N, visible bias N; both biases on by NetKet default, alpha = --features = 1), no weight sharing across translations. samples = 1024 per optimisation step (MCState n_samples = batch_size; MetropolisExchange with n_chains = batch_size = 1024, one sample per chain per step, each separated by sweep_size = N = 16 proposals (NetKet default), n_discard_per_chain = 0); iterations = 10000 ("--max_step" default=10**4); optimizer SR (VMC_SRt when n_parameters >= n_samples), lr 1e-3. The final energy is then estimated once with estim_size = 1024^2 = 1048576 samples (not an optimisation step). NetKet pinned twice by the program: programs/vmc_netket/requirements.txt "NetKet==3.13.0" and conda_env.yaml "netket=3.11.4"; every NetKet line cited here reads the same at both tags. The energy is older than the script: VarBench's data file listed it with no code link ("TODO: own code", varbench/varbench 0ef1497c and 6e9f6b83, 2024-07-11) until the scripts were added on 2024-07-30 (5047bfd6 RBM, d54f7c01 RNN, 765c5d13 GCNN), which changed only the reference column, so the script documents the settings after the fact, with library versions that may postdate the run.

compute.note: Parameters evaluated: NetKet 3.13.0 Jastrow stores the strictly lower triangle of W, N(N-1)/2 = 16*15/2 = 120 real (float32) weights, which is also what vmc.py prints as n_params (tree_size_real_nonzero). Samples: 1024 per SR step, 1024 chains of length 1, each sample one sweep of 16 exchange proposals, no discard. Iterations: 10^4 steps (--max_step default). Driver: nk.VMC with nk.optimizer.SR(QGTOnTheFly) (n_parameters < n_samples). After training the energy is estimated from 2^20 samples. stored sigma 0.0015 vs sqrt(stored variance 2.20818 / 2^20) = 0.0015: consistent with the script's 2^20-sample final estimate (--estim_size default). Provenance: the value entered VarBench in bbcfdc1 (2023-01-15, Dian Wu); the linked script was added to varbench/methods in c686621 (2024-07-30) without the value changing, so the script is the authors' later reconstruction of the baseline, not a log of the run (the same holds for the TFIsing RBM rows, scripts/defects.mjs). The 2^20-sample final estimate is corroborated by the stored sigma; batch size and step count are not independently corroborated. No device or time is recorded (the conda env includes CUDA; the README says a GPU is "usually needed for VMC on larger lattices", which is not a statement about these runs).

compute.reported_as: We use our model with a homogeneous hidden dimension tau = 8 for all layers and angular momenta. We optimize our models through VMC with learning rate eta = 0.001 and N_samples = 4096. Figure 2 shows the computed ground-state energy of the J1-J2 model at different ratios J2/J1 on a 4x4 lattice with periodic boundary conditions || We use 4096 samples to estimate the expectation values in each step. Automatic differentiation [34] via the Jax library backpropagates the gradients through our network, and we use the Adam optimizer with learning rate 0.001. Furthermore, we use gradient clipping with a maximum gradient norm of 0.001. (...) we first carry out a Stochastic Reconfiguration (SR) step with a uniform diagonal shift of magnitude 0.01, followed by a step using the resulting update direction with an Adam optimizer. To save computational resources, in this optimization regime we use 256 samples and learning rate 0.005. Afterwards, we switch to the standard optimization strategy (and drop the SR step). || The software for this work was built on the NetKet library [21]. The computational resources (Stevin Supercomputer Infrastructure) and services used in this work were provided by the VSC (Flemish Supercomputer Center), and the Flemish Government - department EWI.
compute.source: Sec. IV A (4x4 study, Fig. 2); Appendix B Optimization details; Acknowledgments, arXiv:2104.14869 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: The 4x4 energy is from the Fig. 2 scan (tau = 8, eta = 0.001, N_samples = 4096); the paper does not print the 4x4 numbers, VarBench holds them (row reference PRB 104, 045123). Parameter count not given as a number (determined by tau and jmax; no count printed), so parameters left null. No GPU/CPU-hours or wall-clock stated; iterations left null.
